Describe the structure of spell data

Source: R/describe_spells.R
describe_spells.Rd

Spell data, one row per spell with a start and an end, is where register data is most often subtly wrong: spells that overlap, a transfer recorded as two spells, a spell that ends before it starts, a spell that never ends. describe_spells() counts all of it in one pass and judges nothing; require what should hold with ensure_no_overlap().

Usage

describe_spells(data, id, start, end)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble with one row per spell, or a database or Arrow table: see Database tables in checkpoints.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select), e.g. cpr.

start, end

Columns with the first and last day (or period) of each spell. A missing end means an ongoing spell.

Value

An object of class inshape_spells, printed as a summary. It is a list with the counts n_rows, n_spells (usable spells), n_units, n_missing_start, n_end_before_start, n_ongoing, n_single (spells of one day or period) and n_units_overlapping (units with a touching, overlapping, nested or duplicate spell), and the tibbles relations (relation, spells), gaps and lengths (summaries of gap and spell lengths), spells_per_unit (spells, units) and by_year (year, starts, ends; by value for whole numbers).

Details

How each spell relates to the earlier ones

Within a unit, spells are taken in order of start, and each is compared with the latest end among the unit's earlier spells:

  • gap: it starts after a gap. The gap lengths are summarised.

  • adjacent: it starts the day (or period) after an earlier spell ends. Two adjacent spells are often one spell recorded twice, e.g. a transfer between wards or employers, and may need merging with merge_spells() before spells are counted.

  • touching: it starts on the day an earlier spell ends. Spells are closed intervals, so the two share that day and overlap by one day, the usual way a discharge and a readmission on the same day look.

  • overlapping: it starts inside an earlier spell and ends after it.

  • nested: it lies entirely within an earlier spell, or starts after an ongoing one.

  • duplicate: it has the same start and end as the spell before it.

Spells with the same start are taken longest first, so a shorter one is nested in the longer. A missing end means an ongoing spell. Spells with a missing start, or an end before the start, are counted and left out of the rest.

start and end may be dates, compared by day, or whole numbers such as years or month numbers, compared by that unit.

Why it is fast

Units are compressed to integer ids by the compiled engine, the spells are sorted once by data.table's multi-threaded radix sort, and one compiled pass then relates each spell to the earlier ones, reading memory in order. Counts and lengths are read from counts per day, never from sorting millions of values.

See also

merge_spells() to merge adjacent and overlapping spells, ensure_no_overlap() to require spells not to overlap, ensure_no_gaps() to require that they leave no gaps, spells_to_panel() to turn spells into a panel.

Examples

admissions <- data.frame(
  cpr   = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "c"),
  start = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2020-01-11", "2020-03-01",
                    "2020-01-01", "2020-01-05", "2021-06-01")),
  end   = as.Date(c("2020-01-10", "2020-01-20", "2020-03-05",
                    "2020-01-31", "2020-01-10", NA))
)
# a: a transfer on 11 January, then a gap; b: a nested spell; c: ongoing
describe_spells(admissions, cpr, start, end)
#> ── Spells: start to end per cpr ────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 6 rows, 6 usable spells, 3 units
#> 
#> ✔ Every spell has a start and ends after it
#> ⚠ Units with overlapping spells: 1 (33.3%)
#> • Ongoing (no end): 1
#> 
#> Relation to the unit's earlier spells:
#>     relation    spells
#>   1 gap              1
#>   2 adjacent         1
#>   3 touching         0
#>   4 overlapping      0
#>   5 nested           1
#>   6 duplicate        0
#> 
#> Gaps between spells, in days:
#>         n   min   q25 median  mean   q75   max
#>   1     1    40    40     40    40    40    40
#> 
#> Length of ended spells, in days:
#>         n   min   q25 median  mean   q75   max
#>   1     5     5     6     10  12.4    10    31
